Hex World: open questions

2026-10-27, fourth round. A19 to A29 are answered; A30 to A32 are open.

A30B1 boulders and outcrop: built and gated, ready to land

Q1
Approve the five pieces: boulder_granite, _b, _c, _d (2.2 to 4.5 m) and outcrop_granite (8 x 5 x 1.3 m), built from the A25 refs at the approved sizes, scatter densities, coast band and LOD rule. They pass every asset gate. Recommended: approve.
Q2
Rule order. The boulders and outcrop lead their tiles' scatter rules (O1), so every meadow and forest lays out again. Appended after the existing rules instead (O2), earlier props keep their spots, but the outcrop never fits (0 placed in 64 seeds on meadow and on forest). Recommended: O1.
Q3
Thumbnails. Meadow and forest thumbnails now show boulders, and the thumbnail camera aims 2 m higher (look-at 3.5 to 5.5 m) so a spruce tip no longer touches the frame edge. Every thumbnail shifts slightly, as in the comparison below (left: now, right: with B1). Recommended: accept.
Q4
Every-piece check. With boulders sharing the beach's 0 to 6 cap and the forest's rules reordered, the 31-tile mixed world no longer happens to draw beach_driftwood's base variant or log_fallen_c, so the check that every scatter piece draws fails. O1: add a few tiles to the mixed world so every piece draws again. O2: accept the miss for those two. Recommended: O1.
Q5
Smaller defaults as built: no outcrop on the coast band (it never fits), no boulders on beach_outer (none fit), the outcrop's bake at 109 px/m against about 128 (its size at 1024²), and the small boulders ending at 400 m as approved. Recommended: accept.

A31B2 dry-stone walls and hedgerows: references and layout

Q1
Approve refs 1 to 4 (top row) as the look and scale: dry granite walls with an upright cope, the same granite as the boulders, a timber five-bar gate between granite posts, and untrimmed hawthorn and hazel hedges in the matte verge-bush green, one with a hedgerow oak. The image model keeps drawing right-angle corners; hex boundaries meet at 120°, so corners would be built to that spec rather than copied. Recommended: approve as look and scale.
Q2
Sizes. Wall 1.1 m tall, 0.7 m wide at the foot. Hedge 1.9 m tall, 1.5 m wide. Pieces: 4 m straight runs (two variants each), a 2 m end, a 120° bend, a three-way junction, a 4 m gateway (wall), and a 4 m run with an 8 m oak (hedge). A 16 m tile edge is then exactly 2 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 2 m. Recommended: these sizes.
Q3
Where they go. O1: automatic field boundaries on shared tile edges, wherever a farm or wheat tile meets a grass land tile; wall or hedge picked per edge from the world seed, one gate edge per farm. Roads, rivers, rail and coast break them, and you place nothing yourself. O2: boundaries inside the farm tile (the paddock fence already does this). O3: short 4 to 8 m runs as meadow scatter. A per-edge toggle you control could come later; it needs a save-format change. Recommended: O1 now, O3 later.
Q4
Walking: walls and hedges block the walker, gaps pass, a closed gate blocks. Recommended: yes.
Q5
Draw cost: about 40 to 65 more draws at the overview where walls and hedges show. The mixed scatter world now sits at 452 of 500 after the cascade skip, so with B1, B3 and B2 together the overview may pass 500 again; shared scatter materials (A28) would then come back. Recommended: build, measure, and bring the numbers back here.

A32B3 lily pads and reed bed: built and gated, landing now

Q1
Approve the four pieces: lily_cluster (3 pads), lily_cluster_b (7 pads and a white lily), lily_cluster_c (5 pads and a pink bud), all using the spring's own pad so they read as one family, and reed_bed (70 common reed stems, about 3.6 x 1.8 m, 2.4 m tall, swaying in the wind), scattered on river bends, slow straights and springs at the approved densities. They pass every asset gate and are landing now with approval pending. Recommended: approve.
Q2
Far pads. The approval says pads drop out past 400 m, but the gate needs every piece to keep a far LOD. So the far LOD keeps the biggest pads as flat 2-triangle quads (1 of 3, 7 of 7 and 3 of 5). The other way is to let a piece have no far LOD at all, a change across the gate, scatter test and exporter. Recommended: accept as built.
Q3
Reeds on springs are rare: 8 of 168 spring tiles get a reed bed, against 68 of 168 bends, because the spring's granite ring and built-in pads leave little room. O1: accept (reeds mostly on bends). O2: a smaller reed bed variant for springs. Recommended: O1.
Q4
At its largest scale the reed bed's leaning edge plumes can reach past its 1.85 m footprint, over a bank prop or within about 0.8 m of the tile edge. Reducing the lean needs a rebuild. Recommended: accept.
